leads.summary: The new command -v check fails the repository's bin-style test
leads.consequence: Any ./test/shell or ./test/all run hits the bin-style-test.sh rule, prints this receiver's path and exits 1 even though the focused receiver test passes 11/11; base passes. Use the repository's omarchy-cmd-present helper for an optional binary, or reconcile the rule with an explicit exception.

leads.summary: A successful xdg-user-dir lookup with no DOWNLOAD setting silently changes the receiver's default from ~/Downloads to $HOME
leads.consequence: When user-dirs.dirs is missing, has no DOWNLOAD line or has one the updater reset because its directory vanished, the shipped xdg-user-dir exits successfully and prints $HOME. The nonempty test treats that as a configured downloads directory and creates ~/.omarchy-taildrop; files from Taildrop are delivered into the home root instead of ~/Downloads, without a startup error or fallback. On every subsequent service restart the same root is selected until config changes. If #12766 also merges, its Bluetooth receiver defaults to ~/Downloads in precisely this absent-config case, so incoming files from the two transports split destinations. Distinguish an unset DOWNLOAD entry from an explicitly configured $HOME, which users may intend.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; coordinator confirmed upstream v0.20 source; published. #12766 side note unverified, dropped

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the reported case is fixed. With the real `xdg-user-dir` (xdg-user-dirs 0.20-1) and `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR="$HOME/dl"` in `user-dirs.dirs`, the base receiver delivers to `~/Downloads`, while this head delivers to `~/dl` and does not create `~/Downloads`. The new test case passes on this head (11/11) and fails against the base receiver, so it covers the regression it targets.

Two issues remain: the new `command -v` check fails the repo's `bin-style-test.sh`, and the `~/Downloads` fallback does not apply whenever `xdg-user-dir` is installed.

### `bin-style-test.sh` fails on the new `command -v`

`test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh` fails when any `bin/` file other than `omarchy-cmd-*`, `omarchy-pkg-*` or `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` contains `command -v`. The new `elif command -v xdg-user-dir` in `bin/omarchy-tailscale-receive` trips that rule:

```text
base: ok - bin commands use command helpers                  (exit 0)
head: <root>/bin/omarchy-tailscale-receive
      not ok - bin commands use command helpers              (exit 1)
```

**Impact:** `./test/shell` reports a failing file. The "11/11" in the PR description covers only `tailscale-receive-test.sh`.

**Suggested change:** either of these passes both `bin-style-test.sh` and `tailscale-receive-test.sh` (11/11), and each still falls back to `~/Downloads` when `xdg-user-dir` is absent from PATH:
- Replace the `elif` condition with `omarchy-cmd-present xdg-user-dir`, and add `$ROOT/bin` to the new test case's PATH (`PATH="$WORKDIR/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH"`) so the test does not depend on an installed helper.
- Or drop the presence check and turn the `elif` into `else`. The existing `dir=$(xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD 2>/dev/null) || dir=""` already handles a missing binary. `AGENTS.md` asks not to guard commands from the default package set, and `xdg-user-dirs` is present on stock installs (the ISO's fresh-install package manifest lists xdg-user-dirs 0.20-1, and `omarchy-provision-user` calls `xdg-user-dirs-update` unguarded), though it is not a direct dependency of the `omarchy` package.

### With `xdg-user-dir` installed, an unset or reset download dir resolves to `$HOME`, not `~/Downloads`

The PR description calls `~/Downloads` the last resort, and line 26 implements it as a fallback. In practice `[[ -n $dir ]] || dir="$HOME/Downloads"` only takes effect when `xdg-user-dir` is missing (and `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` is empty). The binary prints `$HOME` and exits 0 when no DOWNLOAD entry is configured (upstream v0.20 [`src/xdg-user-dir-lookup.c`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xdg/xdg-user-dirs/-/blob/v0.20/src/xdg-user-dir-lookup.c), `xdg_user_dir_lookup`). Also, at login `xdg-user-dirs-update` rewrites an entry whose directory was deleted to `"$HOME/"` ("… was removed, reassigning DOWNLOAD to homedir").

Real `xdg-user-dir` 0.20-1, fresh fake HOME per case:

| Case | `xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD` | Base receiver | Head receiver |
|---|---|---|---|
| no `user-dirs.dirs` | `$HOME` | `~/Downloads/sent.txt` | `~/sent.txt`, staging `~/.omarchy-taildrop` |
| `~/Downloads` deleted, then `xdg-user-dirs-update` rerun (as at login) | `$HOME/` | `~/Downloads/sent.txt` (dir recreated) | `~/sent.txt`, staging `~/.omarchy-taildrop` |
| custom `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR="$HOME/dl"` | `~/dl` | `~/Downloads` | `~/dl/sent.txt` |

**Impact:** a user who deletes `~/Downloads` without choosing another folder gets Taildrop files loose in the home directory, plus a hidden `~/.omarchy-taildrop`, from the next login on. That matches the XDG rules but not the PR's stated behaviour. The new test stub always prints a custom directory, so it models neither case.

**Suggested change:** decide which behaviour is intended.
- For `~/Downloads`: treat a result equal to `$HOME` as unset, for example `[[ -n $dir && ${dir%/} != "${HOME%/}" ]] || dir="$HOME/Downloads"`, and add a test where the stub prints `$HOME`. In an isolated run (combined with the `else` variant above), no config and `"$HOME/"` both went to `~/Downloads`, custom `~/dl` still went to `~/dl`, and both test files passed. Trade-off: a user who deliberately pointed DOWNLOAD at `$HOME` gets `~/Downloads` recreated, and an exported `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` equal to `$HOME` is overridden too. An explicit argument still wins.
- For `$HOME`: correct the PR text, and consider noting at the fallback line that it only applies when `xdg-user-dir` is missing.

### Interaction with open PRs #13353 and #9277

- **#13353** turns `$WORKDIR/notifications` into a directory. Git merges it with this PR without conflict, but the combined `tailscale-receive-test.sh` then stops at this PR's `: >"$WORKDIR/notifications"` with `Is a directory` (exit 1, no `not ok` line), before this PR's two assertions run. The new case never reads notifications, so deleting that line fixes it. Adding `$ROOT/bin` to the case's PATH also routes its notification through the repo's own notifier. Both variants passed standalone (11/11) and merged (9 `ok`).
- **#9277** also appends cases at the end of `tailscale-receive-test.sh`, which gives a textual conflict there. The two blocks test different things, so a resolution would keep both.

**Documentation:** `manual/35-networking.md`, `shell/plugins/panels/tailscale/README.md` and the echo in `bin/omarchy-install-service-tailscale` still say files land in `~/Downloads`. Something like "your downloads folder (`~/Downloads` by default)" would stay accurate.

**Optional test improvement:** no case checks that an exported `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` still beats `xdg-user-dir`. A mutant replacing the default with `dir="${1:-$(xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD)}"` (the form proposed in #11982) passed all 11 assertions. One more case, appended after the new xdg-user-dir case (it reuses `$xdg_home` and the stub), catches it and passes on this head:

```bash
# An exported XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR still wins over the xdg-user-dir lookup.
envdl="$WORKDIR/envdl"
mkdir -p "$envdl"
printf 'txt' >"$WORKDIR/outbox/exported.txt"

XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR="$envdl" HOME="$xdg_home" PATH="$WORKDIR/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-tailscale-receive" --once

[[ -f $envdl/exported.txt && ! -e $WORKDIR/mydl/exported.txt ]] ||
  fail "taildrop receive prefers an exported XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR" "$(ls "$envdl" "$WORKDIR/mydl")"
pass "taildrop receive prefers an exported XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR"
```

## Review information

**Test scope:** reviewed head `a18e808b`. `tailscale-receive-test.sh` and `bin-style-test.sh` were run in an isolated sandbox at base and head, together with candidate fixes and the combined test files from #13353. The receiver ran against the real `xdg-user-dir` 0.20-1 with stubbed `tailscale` in fake home directories. No desktop session, systemd user manager, uwsm login or live Taildrop transfer was used. The login-time `xdg-user-dirs-update` step was run by hand in a fake HOME, and service environment and ordering were checked from source. The full `./test/shell` suite was not run.
